newsitem.title: AUSTRIA: Austria's ATX index stalls, upward trend intact.
newsitem.headline: Austria's ATX index stalls, upward trend intact.

text.p: Austria's blue-chip ATX index ended unchanged on Thursday, pausing after yesterday's close at a 70-month high to gather energy for another push into record territory, traders said.
"At first one did notice a certain amount of uncertainty lapping over from the U.S. markets. But things then settled down," said one trader.
Strong demand for the ordinary shares of Creditanstalt and OMV helped lift the market out of initial softness with the ATX ending flat at 1,235.79 points.
"When you look at the market environment, we managed to do pretty well," said another trader.
Traders expect the Austrian market's relative resiliency, supported by the German market and the firm Bund future, to continue buoying share prices. "Underlying sentiment is positive," said one.
But another trader warned against too much optimism. "U.S. rates should remain in the back of one's mind. If something happens there, we're not going to be able to disconnect ourselves from it."
The index moved narrowly between 1,233 and 1,239.03 points, with four shares higher, 16 lower, and one unchanged.
Microchip producer Austria Mikro Systeme led the day's decliners, shedding 2.19 percent to 1,159 schillings.
Creditanstalt ordinaries were the best performers, jumping 3.37 percent to 733.9 schillings on catch-up buying following a recent sell-off after the bank was sold to rival Bank Austria last month.
Creditanstalt's preferred were the most actively traded on turnover of 70,383 lots, losing 5.5 schillings to 464.
The broad-based Vienna bourse index gained 0.05 percent to 456.5 points.
The March ATX future ended four points lower at 1,241 on turnover of 1,047 contracts.
